before.label: UK consumer prices (CPI), change over 12 months to August

scenarios.rise: headline beat: CPI up from 3.1%. Then: £100 of everyday shopping a year ago now costs £100 × (1 + CPI) (lumpsum, 1 year). A cast line: Rohan's pay rise of an assumed 3% is now behind prices. Context only, no forecast; the Bank of England decides on 5 Nov.
scenarios.same: headline beat: CPI unchanged at 3.1%. Myth bust: 'inflation stopped' is wrong; prices are still rising 3.1% a year, they just aren't speeding up. £100 basket computed as above.
scenarios.fall: headline beat: CPI down from 3.1%. Myth bust: falling inflation doesn't mean falling prices; the basket still costs more than a year ago, by less. £100 basket computed as above.

maths.name: basket
maths.note: replace rate_pct with the announced CPI figure

notes: Copy the announced figure exactly from the ONS bulletin's main points. Use GBP. No supplier, bank or product named. If the bulletin isn't out by 12:30 IST, stop.
